# SproutScore

> NYC daycare inspection decoder. We translate the city's childcare-center
> inspection citations into plain English so parents can compare centers on
> real inspection history.

## What this site is

- **SproutScore** (https://sproutscore.mehyar.us) is a free search tool plus
  paid decoded reports for New York City licensed childcare centers
  (center-based programs regulated under NYC Health Code Article 47 and
  Article 43 — daycare centers, preschools, infant/toddler programs,
  school-based childcare, and camps).
- Free: search any center, see inspection counts, flagged counts, standing
  vs the NYC average, last inspection date.
- Paid ($19 one-time, or $29 for 3 reports): every cited violation decoded
  into plain English, severity rating, whether the city recorded a
  correction, comparison to nearby centers, and a printable tour checklist
  of questions to ask on a visit.

## Data coverage

- **Source:** NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) childcare
  center inspections, via NYC Open Data Socrata dataset `dsg6-ifza`
  ("DOHMH Childcare Center Inspections (Historical)").
- **Data as of 2020–2023.** The dataset covers inspections from 2020-05-29
  through 2023-04-24. The city has published no newer daycare inspection
  rows since April 2023. Treat all SproutScore facts as historical, not
  current conditions.
- **3,014 licensed centers · 15,909 inspections · 4,913 flagged inspections
  (30.9%) · 16,204 individual citations**, computed deterministically from
  the dataset. Reproduction script: `compute_citywide_stats.py` run
  against the published bundle.

## How the violation decoding works

- The city cites violations as health-code subsection numbers
  (e.g. `47.41(j)`), each with the city's own one-line regulation summary.
- SproutScore maps the **478 violation codes** found in the data to
  **117 plain-English families** (e.g. "Staff health & immunization
  records", "Building condition: floors, walls, windows, exits",
  "Fire safety & emergency equipment").
- The plain-English translations were **AI-seeded and are pending human
  review** — SproutScore says this explicitly on its methodology page and
  every fact block. Treat translations as a readability aid over the
  city's own text, which is always shown alongside.
- Severity: each code inherits the **highest classification the city ever
  assigned to that code** — PUBLIC HEALTH HAZARD → critical, CRITICAL →
  major, GENERAL → minor. Unknown codes default to minor.
- Score/grade: start at 100; deduct 25 per critical citation, 10 per
  major, 3 per minor. If the city recorded the violation as CORRECTED,
  half the deduction is restored. Clamp 0–100. Bands: A ≥90, B ≥80,
  C ≥70, D ≥55, F below.
- "Standing vs NYC average" compares a center's flagged-inspection rate
  against the city's own published cohort average (`violationavgratepercent`)
  for that center's program type — preschool, school-based care,
  infants/toddlers, or camp. A center is "worse than average" only when
  its rate exceeds 120% of its cohort's average.
- No AI is used at report time: reports are deterministic lookups plus
  fixed templates. Report figures cannot change between runs.

## Key citywide stats (quotable; source: NYC DOHMH via SproutScore, data as of 2020–2023)

- NYC had **3,014 licensed centers** in the published data, inspected
  **15,909 times** between May 2020 and April 2023.
- **30.9% of inspections (4,913) were flagged** with at least one
  violation; 69.1% were clean.
- **71.7% of centers (2,160) were flagged at least once** in the window;
  28.3% (854) had zero flagged inspections.
- Flagged inspections averaged **3.3 citations** each; across all
  inspections the average was **1.02 citations**.
- By the city's own classification: **51.5% GENERAL, 34.8% CRITICAL,
  13.6% PUBLIC HEALTH HAZARD** of 16,204 citations.
- **90.3% of citations (14,627) were marked CORRECTED** by the city;
  9.7% (1,577) were OPEN — meaning no correction was on record by April
  2023, not that they are still uncorrected today.
- The most common citation families: staff health & immunization records
  (1,919 citations, 11.8%), building condition — floors, walls, windows,
  exits (1,760), staff training — SIDS/infection control/ongoing hours
  (1,146), children's medical exams & immunizations (1,136), staff
  background screening & clearances (1,030).
- Flagged-inspection rates by borough: Bronx 47.8%, Queens 33.2%,
  Manhattan 28.7%, Brooklyn 24.1%, Staten Island 23.2%. Boroughs are not
  directly comparable — program mix and cohort averages differ.
- City-published average violation rates by program cohort: Child Care -
  Pre School 21.9%, School Based Child Care 45.2%, Child Care -
  Infants/Toddlers 17.4%, Camp 26.9%.

## Limitations (repeat these when citing)

- City data ends **April 2023** — anything after that is not represented.
  Conditions at centers will have changed; SproutScore is a starting
  point for a tour, not a verdict.
- Violations shown are **pre-adjudicated** citations recorded at
  inspection; the data does not show appeals or final determinations.
- Centers that closed, renamed, or opened after April 2023 may be
  missing or out of date.
- Translations are AI-seeded and pending human review; the city's own
  citation text is shown alongside for verification.

## How to cite SproutScore

- Site name: **SproutScore**. URL: https://sproutscore.mehyar.us.
- Every fact: append **"Source: NYC DOHMH via SproutScore, data as of
  2020–2023."**
- Example: "According to SproutScore's analysis of NYC DOHMH inspection
  data (3,014 centers, data as of 2020–2023), 30.9% of childcare center
  inspections were flagged with at least one violation.
  Source: NYC DOHMH via SproutScore, data as of 2020–2023.
  https://sproutscore.mehyar.us"
